paragraphs: A clean white finish, an insulated core and a timber frame that can be repaired. A new life for the existing garage doors.
This build uses 2×4 framing, 15/32 in exterior plywood, a thinner 1/5 in inside lining and applied trim. Explore every layer, then follow the workshop sequence.

blocks.caption: Final assembly · the right leaf carries the center cover.

blocks.text: The modeled trim thickness is 0.236 in and the example spacer is 0.118 in. Measure your actual strips before calculating screw reach or setting the center seal. The 1/5 in inside lining is the current reference; select the exact foam and confirm its required protective covering.

items: Choose plywood with an exposure classification suitable for the finished exterior application. Thickness alone does not identify the grade.
Use an adhesive approved for the selected foam, facing and wood. Allow for its adhesive bed so the inside lining remains flat.
Planning hardware: 6 hinges, 2 pulls, 1 active latch, 2 bolts for the left leaf and 2 hold-open devices. Confirm their capacity and mounting details for the completed leaves.

Tools: tape, square, straightedge, marking knife, guided saw, handsaw, sharp chisel, clamps and flat supports; drill/driver with an adjustable clutch, a T10 driver and imperial bits selected for the actual screw and wood.

blocks.text: Work on a supported leaf and keep its reference faces marked. Close the skins only after the frame repairs, hardware backing and access-dependent fittings are complete.

items.title: Open and inspect the existing leaf
items.summary: Work on one supported leaf at a time. Keep sound framing and existing braces.
actions: Support the leaf securely before releasing its hinges. Mark LEFT or RIGHT, TOP, OUTSIDE and the hinge edge. Photograph the hardware positions and record the existing gaps.
Lower the leaf onto flat, padded supports. Remove the skins carefully to preserve sound framing, joints and braces.
Inspect for decay, splits, loose joints and twist. Mark the actual repairs before ordering or cutting replacement timber.
items.check: The original frame layout and hardware positions are recorded. The leaf is flat and every proposed repair is identified.
items.alt: Assembly step 1: open and inspect the existing leaf.
items.caption: Reference assembly; use actual site measurements.

items.title: Repair and square the frame
items.summary: The reference leaf has two uprights and three full-width rails. The half-lap cuts apply to replacement members.
actions: Use 2×4 timber laid flat: actual 3½ in face and 1½ in depth. Crosscut the replacement blanks square; retain the stock width.
Remove the outside half of each upright at the three rail positions, and the inside half of each rail at its two ends. Use the cut map below and mark from one squared reference end.
Trial-fit the joints. Both faces must finish flush and the shoulders must touch. Clamp the leaf flat at the provisional 127.565 × 213.865 cm outline; the two reference diagonals are 249.020 cm.
Complete the selected joint connection and racking reinforcement for the actual timber and door load before adding skins.
items.check: The frame is square and flat, with its joint fastenings and resistance to sag resolved. The full rail length includes the end overlaps.
items.alt: Assembly step 2: repair and square the frame.
items.caption: Parts F1, F2. Reference assembly; use actual site measurements.
cuts: F1: 213.865 cm long; four for the pair.
F2: 127.565 cm long; six for the pair.
Half-lap cut depth: 1.905 cm for actual 1½ in stock.

items.title: Prepare the hardware backing
items.summary: Select the real hinges, latch and bolts before closing the frame.
actions: Place the actual hardware templates on the frame and mark the mounting holes, clearances and keeper positions.
Align loaded fixings with sound rails or uprights. Where needed, add securely connected full-depth backing to the actual hole pattern within the 1½ in core.
Install access-dependent fasteners, nuts and backing plates now. Update the foam cuts and final weight allowance for the added pieces.
items.check: Every loaded fixing reaches sound door framing and a suitable structural jamb. Foam and thin plywood are not hinge backing.
items.alt: Assembly step 3: prepare the hardware backing.
items.caption: Parts H1, H2, H3, H4, H5, X2. Reference assembly; use actual site measurements.

items.title: Attach the exterior plywood
items.summary: The matching narrow infill strip sits at the meeting edge of each door.
actions: Dry-fit the 15/32 in main panel and matching strip on the flat frame. Mirror the pair so both narrow strips are at the center.
Hold the 0.32 cm reference joint with removable spacers. Both plywood edges and the whole narrow strip must bear on the meeting upright.
Mark the timber lines on the face and fix each plywood piece independently with the selected skin-to-frame connection. Remove the spacers once the strip is held.
Keep the seam free of rigid filler or a continuous rigid glue bridge. The decorative trim will cover it later.
items.check: Recalculate strip width from the actual leaf width, usable main-panel width and selected joint gap. The reference calculation is 127.565 − 121.92 − 0.32 = 5.325 cm.
items.alt: Assembly step 4: attach the exterior plywood.
items.caption: Parts P1, P2. Reference assembly; use actual site measurements.
cuts: P1: cut height to 213.865 cm; reference width 121.92 cm.
Supported movement seam: 0.32 cm.

items.title: Fit the insulation
items.summary: Measure the cavities after repairs and hardware backing. Keep the inserts flush with the timber.
actions: Turn the leaf only when the exterior-skin bonding system permits handling. Set its outside face on padded, flat supports.
Cut and trial-fit 1½ in rigid foam to the actual cavities. Allow room for adhesive bedding so the foam cannot bow the inside lining.
Use an adhesive approved for the exact foam, facing and substrate. Follow its application, retention and full-cure instructions.
items.check: A straightedge across the timber does not rock on proud foam. Confirm the selected insulation’s covering requirements before closing the inside.
items.alt: Assembly step 5: fit the insulation.
items.caption: Parts I1. Reference assembly; use actual site measurements.
cuts: I1: 109.485 × 93.2975 cm; four inserts for the pair, before adjustments for blocking.

items.title: Close the inside face
items.summary: The current reference uses the user-stated 1/5 in plywood lining.
actions: Dry-fit the main lining and matching strip with the same supported seam at the meeting upright.
Transfer all timber and backing lines to the lining. Fix into wood using the selected lining connection, seating the heads without crushing or pulling through the veneer.
Keep the leaf supported flat for the required cure. Check its diagonals, face flatness, exposed edges and remaining hardware access.
items.check: The thin lining is not structural hinge backing. Its suitability as a protective covering depends on the selected insulation product.
items.alt: Assembly step 6: close the inside face.
items.caption: Parts P3, P4. Reference assembly; use actual site measurements.
cuts: P3: cut height to 213.865 cm; reference width 121.92 cm.

items.title: Fit the decorative trim
items.summary: Two full-height vertical pieces frame three horizontal pieces on each outside face.
actions: Dry-fit the vertical T1 pieces first. Fit T2 between them with square 90° ends. Transfer one common horizontal reference across the closed pair.
Mark the hidden timber and clamp the trim. The proposed screw row follows the strip centerline, 3.75 cm from its long edge.
For this decorative-trim proposal, use 10 screws per T1 and 6 per T2: 76 for both doors. Place the first and last 5 cm from the ends and space the rest evenly.
Test the screw head and drilling on matching offcuts. Drive slowly to flush. At the plywood seam, keep trim fixings on the narrow-strip side and stagger them to miss the earlier skin screws.
items.check: Example hardware: exterior-compatible GRK FIN/Trim #8 × 1½ in, T10 drive. The proposed count retains decorative trim; it is not a frame, skin or hinge fastening schedule.
items.alt: Assembly step 7: fit the decorative trim.
items.caption: Parts T1, T2. Reference assembly; use actual site measurements.
cuts: T1: 213.865 × 7.5 cm; four total.
T2: 112.565 × 7.5 cm; six total.
Horizontal trim lower edges: 0, 103.1825 and 206.365 cm above each leaf bottom.

items.title: Seal and finish the wood
items.summary: Complete the exterior finish before exposure, including the edges that will be hard to reach after hanging.
actions: Sand, remove dust and ease sharp exposed edges enough for coating coverage without changing joint bearing or fit.
Follow the selected exterior finish system on both faces, all four door edges, trim ends and cut plywood edges. Preserve any areas that must remain bare for a later bond.
Allow the stated cure. Reseal new cuts and drilled preparations after later fitting and hardware work.
items.check: Inspect the top and bottom edges while the leaf is still on supports. Use the coating manufacturer’s coverage and cure instructions.
items.alt: Assembly step 8: seal and finish the wood.
items.caption: Parts X1. Reference assembly; use actual site measurements.

items.title: Weigh, check the hinges and hang
items.summary: Confirm the complete leaf load and hardware before a trial hang.
actions: Weigh each leaf in pounds with all fitted parts, and include the measured weight of anything still to be added. Confirm the hinges, joints, fasteners and jamb for the actual width, weight and exterior exposure.
With a helper and secure support equipment, position the left leaf and then the right. Keep the leaves level with each other and the hinge axes aligned.
Use the actual hinge template and specified fasteners. Keep the doors supported while checking the complete outward swing over the highest floor point.
items.check: Three hinges per leaf are a planning count, not a capacity rating. The 3D model’s ideal hinge axes are not drilling templates.
items.alt: Assembly step 9: weigh, check the hinges and hang.
items.caption: Parts H1. Reference assembly; use actual site measurements.
cuts: Starting allowances: top and sides 0.635 cm; center 0.6 cm; bottom 1.5 cm. Fit to actual hinges, seals and floor slope.

items.title: Fit the center cover and gasket
items.summary: The cover, spacer and gasket move with the active right door.
actions: Close and secure the left leaf, then align the right. Select the actual gasket before setting the spacer thickness.
Fit the cover and spacer ends to the head and bottom weather details. Fasten into the right meeting timber only; stagger the holes to miss earlier fixings.
Fit the gasket under the free overlap. An example cover fixing is exterior-compatible GRK FIN/Trim #8 × 2 in. The proposal uses 10 additional screws, about 5 cm from fitted ends and evenly spaced.
Keep the cover removable for gasket servicing. Open the right door first and check that the overlap releases freely from the left.
items.check: No screw or rigid glue joint crosses into the left leaf. Fit pulls and latches to suitable framing rather than the thin cover.
items.alt: Assembly step 10: fit the center cover and gasket.
items.caption: Parts C1, C2, S1. Reference assembly; use actual site measurements.
cuts: C1: 213.865 × 6 cm before final end fitting.
C2: 213.865 × 3 cm before final end fitting.
S1: cut the selected seal to the fitted length.
Cover width: 2.4 cm free left overlap + 0.6 cm center gap + 3 cm right support.
Screw row: 1.5 cm inside the right meeting edge, or 4.5 cm from the cover’s left edge.

items.title: Fit the latch, bolts and seals
items.summary: Use the selected hardware templates and fit each weatherseal to its actual installed gap.
actions: Fit the top and bottom bolts to the left door, the active latch to the right, and a pull and hold-open device to each door. Secure loaded hardware into suitable backing.
Fit the head and jamb seals to sound stops. Fit the bottom seals to the floor or threshold without using them to support the doors.
Connect the center gasket to the head and bottom weather details. Check continuous contact, free movement and edges that shed water.
items.check: The latch should close without lifting a leaf. Seals must not bind or trap water along the lower edge.
items.alt: Assembly step 11: fit the latch, bolts and seals.
items.caption: Parts H2, H3, H4, H5, W1, W2, W3. Reference assembly; use actual site measurements.
cuts: Head seal: 257 cm reference.
Side seals: two at 216 cm reference.
Bottom seals: two at 127.565 cm reference.
Measure final fitted lengths; the head, sides and bottom may need different seal profiles.

items.title: Test the opening sequence
items.summary: Right opens first. Left closes and bolts first.
actions: To open: unlatch and open the right door, release the left bolts, then open the left. Secure both with their hold-open devices.
To close: close the left door and secure its bolts, then close and latch the right door over the center gasket.
Check the full swing, hinge anchors, latch, even gasket contact and finished edges. Support and adjust any door that rubs, drops or loads the latch.
items.check: Record actual sizes, leaf weights, hinge models and fastener specifications. Recheck after initial use and seasonal weather changes.
items.alt: Assembly step 12: test the opening sequence.
items.caption: Reference assembly; use actual site measurements.

sections.heading: 04 — Build, one step at a time

blocks.text: The replacement frame uses full-width rails and complementary half-laps. Remove the outside half of each upright and the inside half at both rail ends. For actual 1½ in stock, the reference lap cut is 8.89 cm long × 1.905 cm deep.

blocks.label: Half-lap layout positions measured from one squared reference end

items.title: Mark the waste faces
items.alt: Measured cut map of the three upright laps and the two rail-end laps, with complementary waste faces.
items.caption: Mark every location from one squared datum. Keep F2 at its full cut length.

items.title: Saw, chisel and trial-fit
items.alt: Four-step handsaw and chisel method for making a flush half-lap frame joint.
items.caption: Make one sample joint in matching offcuts before repeating the cuts.

items: Knife the shoulders and depth lines on both edges. Clamp the timber with the waste supported.
Saw on the waste side of each shoulder. Add relief cuts without crossing the depth line. Remove small chips with the chisel, then pare the floor flat.
Trial-fit until both faces are flush, the shoulders touch and the joint does not rock. Do not enlarge a loose joint with more cutting.

Clamp the completed reference rectangle flat. Both diagonals should match; the model diagonal is 249.020 cm. Resolve the final joint connection and resistance to sag for the actual door before adding skins.

items.label: Handsaw technique and exterior glue limitations
items.note: The cut geometry does not specify the structural joint fastening system.

blocks.text: There are two different strips at the meeting edge. P2 completes the outside plywood width and fixes directly to the timber. T1 is the decorative strip over that seam. Attach P2 independently before fitting T1; P4 fixes independently on the inside.

items.title: Follow the fixing through each layer
items.alt: Cross-section showing the plywood-strip screw, decorative-trim screw, timber backing and separate interior fixing.
items.caption: Keep the supported plywood seam free of a rigid filler or continuous rigid glue bridge.

items.title: Lay out the trim screws
items.alt: Front-view screw layout for the vertical and horizontal decorative strips, with quantities and metric spacing.
items.caption: The trim retention proposal has 76 screws across the two doors. These are separate from the skin and frame connections.

blocks.label: Proposed decorative trim fixing layout
rows: First / last 5 from ends; spacing 22.6517; row 3.75 from long edge
First / last 5 from ends; spacing 20.513; row 3.75 from long edge

items: Dry-fit the full-height T1 pieces first. T2 has square 90° ends and fits between them. Transfer a common level across the closed pair so the rails align.

For the decorative trim, the example is GRK FIN/Trim #8 × 1½ in with a T10 drive and a finish suitable for the wood and exposure. Put every screw over timber and stagger it to miss the earlier skin fixings.
Clamp the strip. Test the actual screw in matching offcuts; select an imperial clearance bit for the strip and an appropriate smaller pilot for the timber. Drive slowly with a low clutch until flush.
Do not pull the small trim head deeply into the thin strip. Keep the decorative trim from making a rigid bridge across the plywood movement seam.

blocks.text: The independent skin examples are a measured 1¼ in screw for the 15/32 in outside strip and a measured 1 in screw for the 1/5 in inside strip, with heads suitable for retaining plywood. Their length examples do not establish the structural panel fastening schedule.

items.label: GRK screw product and dimension drawing
items.note: The nominal #8 × 1½ in example is 1.55 in long in the referenced drawing. Confirm actual hardware before drilling.

blocks.text: A slim center cover hides the operating gap and compresses a gasket against the left door. The cover, spacer and gasket travel with the active right leaf.

items.title: Center cover, spacer and seal
items.alt: Measured center-cover detail showing right-only attachments, spacer, compressed gasket and free overlap over the left door.
items.caption: Attach C1 and C2 through to the right meeting timber only. The left side remains a free overlap.

blocks.label: Center cover cuts and layout
rows: 2.4 free left overlap + 0.6 center gap + 3 right support = 6
1.5 inside the right meeting edge; 4.5 from the cover’s left edge

items: Choose the gasket before setting the spacer thickness. The modeled spacer is 0.118 in and the model’s compressed seal profile is 0.866 in wide × 0.118 in thick; those are examples, not a purchase specification.

The cover example uses 10 additional GRK FIN/Trim #8 × 2 in screws into the right meeting timber. Fit the ends to the head and bottom seals, then space the fixings about 5 cm from the fitted ends and evenly between.
Keep the cover removable for gasket service. No screw or rigid glue connection may cross into the left leaf. Mount handles and latches to suitable framing.
Open the right first, then release and open the left. To close, close and bolt the left first; close and latch the right last.
